# Themis Phase 0 Specification

2026-10-08 · Sebastian Hansson

This spec turns the kernel in the Themis Foundation Design into buildable detail: the attributes of every kernel entity, a state machine for every document type in Phases 0 to 2, and the posting profile that maps each posting event to accounts. Claude Code builds the kernel from it. Rule IDs (P-, R-, D-) refer to the foundation doc unless this spec introduces them.

## Conventions

Every entity carries the common fields below (append-only entities omit the updated and version fields), uses exact decimal types and time-ordered UUIDs. The attribute tables in the next sections list only entity-specific fields.

**Common fields on every entity**

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID v7 | Generated by the application; time-ordered for index locality; never reused. |
| `created_at`, `created_by` | Timestamp, user | Set once. |
| `updated_at`, `updated_by` | Timestamp, user | Master data and documents, including status changes. Ledger entries are never updated (R-LED-01). |
| `version` | Integer | Incremented on every change; a stale update is rejected (R-API-02). |
| `extension` | JSON | Customer-specific fields only (R-EXT-01); core logic never reads it. |

**Data types**

| Type | PostgreSQL storage | Use and rule |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `text`, 1 to 40 characters: A to Z, 0 to 9, dash, underscore | Business keys such as company code and item number. Stored uppercase. |
| Name | `text`, up to 200 characters | Display names and descriptions. |
| Quantity | `numeric(20,6)` | Entered values are limited further by the unit's decimals. |
| Money | `numeric(20,4)` plus a currency code | Rounded to the currency's minor unit at the defined points only (R-MON-02). |
| UnitPrice | `numeric(20,6)` | Price per price unit; may carry more decimals than money. |
| Cost | `numeric(28,10)` | Unit and average cost. Computed values are rounded half away from zero to 10 decimals when stored and are informational; costing uses value / quantity (moving average algorithm). |
| Rate | `numeric(20,10)` | Exchange rates. |
| Percent | `numeric(7,4)` | 25 % is stored as 25.0000. |
| Date | `date` | Business dates in the company's time zone (R-TIME-01). |
| Timestamp | `timestamptz` | Stored in UTC. |
| Enum | `text` with a check constraint | Allowed values are listed in the attribute tables. |
| CountryCode, CurrencyCode, UnitCode | `text` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, ISO 4217, UN/ECE Recommendation 20. |

**Effective dating.** Effective-dated entities carry `valid_from` (inclusive) and `valid_to` (exclusive; empty means open-ended). Periods for the same business key never overlap; the database enforces this with an exclusion constraint (R-MD-02).

**Notation in the attribute tables.** Req: Y = required, N = optional, D = derived by the system and never entered. PD = personal data under GDPR. An arrow (→) means a reference to another entity.

## Organisation entities

Four entities set the boundaries: an installation holds one company group's companies, a company holds sites, a site holds warehouses. There is no tenant identifier (D-28). A company's base currency and time zone cannot change after its first posting.

**Installation** (one per company group)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | Code | Y | Identifies the installation, for example in exports and integrations. |
| `name` | Name | Y |  |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Suspended | Y | Suspended rejects every command. |
| `default_locale` | text (BCP 47, for example sv-SE) | Y | Default language and formats. |

**Company**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | Code | Y | Unique per installation. |
| `party_id` | → Party | Y | The company's own party record; holds its addresses and contacts. |
| `legal_name` | Name | Y |  |
| `organisation_number` | text | Y | Format validated by the country's localisation. |
| `vat_number` | text | N | Required when the company is VAT registered. |
| `country_code` | CountryCode | Y |  |
| `base_currency` | CurrencyCode | Y | Immutable after the first posting. |
| `time_zone` | text (IANA, for example Europe/Stockholm) | Y | Immutable after the first posting. |
| `fiscal_year_start_month` | integer 1 to 12 | Y |  |
| `chart_of_accounts_id` | → ChartOfAccounts | Y |  |
| `rounding_mode` | Enum: HalfAwayFromZero, HalfEven | Y | Default HalfAwayFromZero. |
| `tax_rounding_level` | Enum: Line, Document | Y | Pending decision D-10. |
| `payment_tolerance` | Money | N | Maximum payment difference written off automatically (R-O2C-07). |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Inactive | Y | Lifecycle in State machines, part 1. |

**Site**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `code` | Code | Y | Unique per company. |
| `name` | Name | Y |  |
| `address_id` | → Address | N | An address of the company's own party. |
| `time_zone` | text (IANA) | N | Defaults to the company's time zone. |

**Warehouse**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `site_id` | → Site | Y | Company is derived from the site. |
| `code` | Code | Y | Unique per company. |
| `name` | Name | Y |  |
| `is_default` | boolean | Y | At most one default warehouse per site. |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Blocked, Inactive | Y | Blocked accepts no new movements. |

## Party entities

A Party exists once per installation; what a company does with it (sell, buy, ship) lives on a PartyRole per company. Commercial terms therefore differ per company without duplicating the customer.

**Party**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `party_number` | Code | Y | From an installation-level number series; unique per installation. |
| `party_type` | Enum: Organisation, Person | Y | A Person party is personal data as a whole. |
| `name` | Name | Y | PD when the party is a Person. |
| `organisation_number` | text | N | Used in the duplicate check. |
| `vat_number` | text | N | Required for zero-rated EU sales. |
| `country_code` | CountryCode | Y |  |
| `language` | text (BCP 47) | N | Language of documents sent to the party. |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Blocked, Inactive | Y | Lifecycle in State machines, part 1. |
| `duplicate_key` | text | D | Normalised organisation number, VAT number, name and postal code (R-MD-01). |
| `anonymised_at` | Timestamp | D | Set when personal data is erased (R-MD-03). |

**PartyRole**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `party_id` | → Party | Y |  |
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `role_type` | Enum: Customer, Supplier, Carrier | Y | Unique per party, company and role type. |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Blocked, Inactive | Y | Blocked: no new documents and no release. |
| `currency` | CurrencyCode | Y | Default document currency. |
| `payment_terms_id` | → PaymentTerms | Y | Customer and supplier roles. |
| `price_list_id` | → PriceList | N | Customer price list (R-O2C-06). |
| `credit_limit` | Money | Y for customers | 0 means every release goes to Credit blocked (R-O2C-01). |
| `party_posting_group` | Enum: Domestic, EU, NonEU | Y | Key for account mapping and tax rules. |
| `vat_status` | Enum: Registered, NotRegistered | Y | Input to tax rules (R-TAX-01). |
| `incoterm`, `incoterm_place` | text (Incoterms 2020 code), text | N | Default delivery terms. |
| `default_bill_to_address_id`, `default_ship_to_address_id` | → Address | N |  |
| `complete_delivery_only` | boolean | Y | Default false (R-O2C-03). |
| `over_delivery_tolerance_pct` | Percent | Y | Default 0 (R-DOC-03). |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N | Effective dating. |

**Address**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `party_id` | → Party | Y |  |
| `purposes` | Set of: Legal, BillTo, ShipTo | Y | At least one. |

| `postal_code`, `city` | text | Y |  |
| `region` | text | N |  |
| `country_code` | CountryCode | Y | Input to tax rules via the ship-to address. |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N | Effective dating. |

**Contact**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `party_id` | → Party | Y |  |
| `name` | Name | Y | PD. |
| `email`, `phone` | text | N | PD. |
| `job_title` | text | N |  |
| `purposes` | Set of: Ordering, Invoicing, Delivery, Certificates | N | Who receives which document. |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Inactive | Y |  |

## Item and unit entities

Item identity is installation-wide, while settings that differ between companies sit on ItemCompany (D-43). Base unit, lot tracking and pack factors freeze once used, because posted history depends on them. Ten entities cover items, their company settings, units, attributes, lots and customer part numbers.

**Item**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_number` | Code | Y | Unique per installation (R-MD-05). |
| `description` | Name | Y |  |
| `item_type` | Enum: Stocked, NonStocked, Service | Y | Only Stocked items create inventory entries. |
| `base_unit` | UnitCode | Y | Immutable after the first inventory entry. |
| `lot_tracking` | Enum: None, Required | Y | Immutable after the first inventory entry. |
| `attribute_template_id` | → AttributeTemplate | N |  |
| `net_weight_kg` | Quantity | N | Per base unit, for example 0.0118 kg per piece. |
| `sales_multiple` | Quantity | N | In base unit. Order quantities round up to a multiple, with a warning. |
| `min_order_qty` | Quantity | N | In base unit. |

**ItemCompany** (one row per item and company, D-43)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id`, `company_id` | → Item, → Company | Y | Unique pair (R-MD-05). An item can be used in a company only through an Active row. |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Blocked, Inactive | Y | Master data lifecycle, per company. |
| `item_posting_group` | Code | Y | Key for account mapping, for example TRADE_GOODS. |
| `tax_class` | Enum: Standard, Reduced, Zero, Exempt | Y | Input to tax rules (R-TAX-01). |
| `costing_method` | Enum: MovingAverage | Y | Only value in v1 (R-INV-05). Master data; never stored on the ItemCostState cache. |
| `sales_allowed`, `purchase_allowed` | boolean | Y | Default true. |
| `default_warehouse_id` | → Warehouse | N | Must belong to the company. |
| `default_sales_unit`, `default_purchase_unit` | UnitCode | N | Must exist as an ItemUnit of the item. |

Planning and replenishment parameters are added to ItemCompany with the Phase 1 purchasing specification.

Item has no status of its own (D-43). There is no installation-wide block: retiring an item means deactivating its ItemCompany row in every company. R-MD-05 still applies to the item number per installation, whatever the status of its ItemCompany rows.

**UnitOfMeasure** (global reference list)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | UnitCode | Y | For example H87 (piece), KGM (kilogram), MTR (metre). |
| `name` | Name | Y |  |
| `dimension` | Enum: Count, Mass, Length, Volume, Time | Y |  |
| `decimals` | integer 0 to 6 | Y | Precision for entered quantities: H87 = 0, KGM = 3. |

**UnitConversion** (global, within one dimension)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_unit`, `to_unit` | UnitCode | Y | Both in the same dimension. |
| `factor` | Rate | Y | 1 from_unit = factor x to_unit, for example 1 KGM = 1000 GRM. |

**ItemUnit** (pack levels per item)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | → Item | Y |  |
| `unit_code` | text | Y | A UnitCode or a pack code such as BOX or CARTON; the same code may have different factors on different items. |
| `factor_to_base` | Rate | Y | Greater than 0. 1 BOX = 200 H87 means 200. Immutable once used on a posted document (R-UOM-01). |
| `purposes` | Set of: Sales, Purchase | Y |  |

**AttributeTemplate**, **AttributeDefinition**, **ItemAttributeValue**

| Entity | Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AttributeTemplate | `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y | One per product family, for example HEX_SCREW. |
| AttributeDefinition | `template_id` | → AttributeTemplate | Y |  |
| AttributeDefinition | `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y | Code unique per template, for example THREAD, LENGTH, STRENGTH_CLASS, FINISH, STANDARD. |
| AttributeDefinition | `data_type` | Enum: Text, Number, Boolean, Choice, Measure | Y |  |
| AttributeDefinition | `unit_code` | UnitCode | N | Required for Measure, for example MMT for length. |
| AttributeDefinition | `choices` | List of text | N | Required for Choice, for example 8.8, 10.9, A2-70. |
| AttributeDefinition | `is_required`, `sort_order` | boolean, integer | Y |  |
| ItemAttributeValue | `item_id`, `definition_id` | → Item, → AttributeDefinition | Y | Unique pair; the definition must belong to the item's template. |
| ItemAttributeValue | `value` | typed per data_type | Y | Validated against data type, unit and choices. |

**Lot**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | → Item | Y | Item must have lot_tracking = Required. |
| `lot_number` | Code | Y | Unique per item. |
| `heat_number`, `supplier_lot_number` | text | N | Traceability to the steel melt and the supplier. |
| `manufactured_on`, `expires_on` | Date | N |  |
| `certificate_attachment_id` | → Attachment | N | For example an EN 10204 3.1 certificate. |
| `status` | Enum: Released, Blocked | Y | Stock in a Blocked lot is not available (R-INV-04). |

**CustomerItemReference**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `party_role_id` | → PartyRole (Customer) | Y |  |
| `item_id` | → Item | Y |  |
| `customer_item_number` | text | Y | Unique per customer role. Printed on order confirmations and invoices. |
| `customer_description` | Name | N |  |

## Commercial and tax entities

Eight entities hold money terms, bank accounts, VAT and prices. Two choices keep v1 deterministic: exactly one tax rule must match a line (R-TAX-03), and a price list is only used in its own currency, with no implicit conversion.

**Currency** and **ExchangeRate**

| Entity | Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Currency | `code`, `name` | CurrencyCode, Name | Y |  |
| Currency | `minor_units` | integer 0 to 3 | Y | SEK and EUR = 2. Drives rounding (R-MON-02). |
| ExchangeRate | `from_currency`, `to_currency` | CurrencyCode | Y |  |
| ExchangeRate | `rate_date` | Date | Y |  |
| ExchangeRate | `rate` | Rate | Y | 1 from_currency = rate x to_currency. |
| ExchangeRate | `rate_type` | Enum: Daily, Manual | Y | Unique per currency pair, date and type. |
| ExchangeRate | `source` | text | N | For example the central bank feed name. |

A document uses the latest Daily rate on or before its document date and stores it (R-MON-03). No rate found: the command is rejected.

**PaymentTerms**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y | For example NET30. |
| `net_days` | integer | Y |  |
| `basis` | Enum: DocumentDate, EndOfMonth | Y | Due date = basis date + net_days. Cash discounts are out of scope for v1. |

**BankAccount**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y |  |
| `iban`, `bic`, `account_number` | text | N | At least one of iban or account_number. |
| `currency` | CurrencyCode | Y |  |
| `gl_account_id` | → Account | Y | The BANK account role resolves here (see Posting profile). |
| `status` | Enum: Active, Inactive | Y |  |

**TaxCode**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y | For example SE25, SE_EU_GOODS, SE_EXPORT. |
| `rate` | Percent | Y | 25.0000 or 0.0000. |
| `tax_type` | Enum: Output, Input | Y | Input is used from Phase 2. |
| `reporting_code` | text | N | VAT return box; supplied by the localisation package. |
| `invoice_note` | text | N | Text the invoice must carry, for example the reason a sale is zero-rated. |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N | A rate change is a new validity period, never an edit. |

**TaxRule**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `direction` | Enum: Sales, Purchase | Y |  |
| `ship_to_scope` | Enum: Domestic, EU, NonEU | Y | Derived per line from company country and ship-to country. In v1 goods ship from the company's own country. |
| `party_vat_status` | Enum: Registered, NotRegistered, Any | Y |  |
| `item_tax_class` | Enum: Standard, Reduced, Zero, Exempt | Y |  |
| `tax_code_id` | → TaxCode | Y |  |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N |  |

Exactly one rule must match a line on its posting date. Zero or several matches is a configuration error and the command is rejected (R-TAX-03).

**PriceList** and **PriceListLine**

| Entity | Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PriceList | `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| PriceList | `code`, `name` | Code, Name | Y |  |
| PriceList | `scope` | Enum: Base, Customer, Agreement | Y | One active Base list per company and currency. |
| PriceList | `party_role_id` | → PartyRole | N | Required when scope = Agreement. |
| PriceList | `currency` | CurrencyCode | Y | Used only for documents in this currency. |
| PriceList | `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `status` | Date, Date, Enum: Active, Inactive | Y, N, Y |  |
| PriceListLine | `price_list_id`, `item_id` | → PriceList, → Item | Y |  |
| PriceListLine | `unit_code` | text | Y | An ItemUnit of the item. |
| PriceListLine | `price_unit_qty` | Quantity | Y | Default 1; 100 means "price per 100". |
| PriceListLine | `unit_price` | UnitPrice | Y |  |
| PriceListLine | `min_qty` | Quantity | Y | Quantity break in the line's unit; default 0. |
| PriceListLine | `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N | No overlap for the same list, item, unit and min_qty. |

**Price resolution** (R-O2C-06): search the customer's Agreement list, then the customer's price list, then the Base list, and stop at the first list with a valid line. Within a list, take the line with the highest min_qty that does not exceed the order quantity. Line net amount = quantity / price_unit_qty x unit_price x (1 - discount %), rounded per R-MON-02.

## Document framework entities

Every business document shares one header, one line and one link model; fields that only one document type needs live in a one-to-one extension table per type (D-16). The kernel's document framework owns the shared tables, the state machine engine and numbering; each extension table belongs to the module that owns the document type, in that module's schema (D-39). Document types are registered in a table (D-40). This spec covers eleven document types: the kernel documents of Phase 0 and the sales-side documents of Phases 1 and 2. Purchasing documents (purchase order and goods receipt in Phase 1; supplier invoice and payment in Phase 2) are specified separately.

**DocumentType** (table-driven registry, system-owned in v1, D-40)

| Code | Number assigned | Gapless | Posts inventory | Posts GL | Party role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MANUAL_JOURNAL | On post | Yes | No | Yes | None |
| INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT | On post | No | Yes | Yes | None |
| STOCK_STATUS_CHANGE | On post | No | Yes | No | None |
| SALES_ORDER | On create | No | No | No | Customer |
| DELIVERY | On create | No | Yes | Yes | Customer |
| CUSTOMER_INVOICE | On post | Yes | No | Yes | Customer |
| CREDIT_NOTE | On post | Yes | No | Yes | Customer |
| CUSTOMER_PAYMENT | On post | No | No | Yes | Customer |
| CUSTOMER_RETURN | On create | No | Yes | Yes | Customer |
| VAT_SETTLEMENT | On post | Yes | No | Yes | None |
| OPENING_OPEN_ITEMS | On post | Yes | No | Yes | Customer, per line |

Manual journals are gapless because they are accounting vouchers. Journal entries themselves are also numbered gapless per fiscal year (see Ledger entities).

**Event names (D-44).** Every state change writes one outbox event, so a command writes one event for each document or master data row whose state it changes. The event is named TYPE plus the command in past tense, schema version 1: ITEM_CREATED, INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT_CREATED, INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT_DISCARDED. Where the state machine tables below give a business name for a transition (for example GOODS_ISSUED for DELIVERY.CONFIRM_SHIPMENT, or INVENTORY_ADJUSTED for INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT.POST), the registry records it per document type, command and resulting state (so SALES_ORDER.RELEASE can yield SALES_ORDER_RELEASED or SALES_ORDER_CREDIT_BLOCKED), and code reads it from there. Master data commands always use the generated name. Business payloads are specified only for events that integrations consume; every other payload carries the id and the changed fields.

**NumberSeries**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id`, `document_type` | → Company, Code | Y |  |
| `prefix` | text | N | For example INV-. |
| `scope` | Enum: Continuous, PerFiscalYear | Y |  |
| `fiscal_year_id` | → FiscalYear | N | Required when scope = PerFiscalYear. |
| `next_number`, `padding` | integer | Y |  |
| `gapless` | boolean | Y | Copied from the document type; cannot be switched off where the type requires it. |

A gapless number is taken inside the posting transaction under a row lock on the series. If the transaction fails, the number returns with it, so no gap appears (R-DOC-07). Other series may use a database sequence, where gaps are allowed. Journal entries number from a series with document type JOURNAL_ENTRY, scope PerFiscalYear, gapless.

**Document** (header, all types)

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id`, `document_type` | → Company, Code | Y |  |
| `document_number` | text | D | Assigned at the type's assignment point; unique per company and type. |
| `draft_reference` | text | D | Temporary reference shown before numbering (R-DOC-04). |
| `status` | Enum, per type | Y | Changes only through the type's state machine (R-DOC-01). |
| `party_role_id` | → PartyRole | N | Required where the type names a party role. |
| `document_date` | Date | Y |  |
| `posting_date` | Date | N | Required at posting; must fall in an open period (R-LED-04). |
| `currency` | CurrencyCode | Y |  |
| `exchange_rate` | Rate | D | Stored at release or posting (R-MON-03). |
| `bill_to_snapshot`, `ship_to_snapshot` | JSON | D | Address copied at release (R-DOC-05). |
| `external_reference` | text | N | For example the customer's PO number. |
| `warehouse_id` | → Warehouse | N | Default for lines. |
| `total_net`, `total_tax`, `total_gross` | Money | D |  |
| `posted_at`, `posted_by` | Timestamp, user | D |  |
| `reason` | text | N | Required by cancel, close-short and reverse commands. |
| `reversal_of_document_id` | → Document | N | Set on a reversal document. |

## Ledger entities

Twelve entities hold the books. JournalEntry, JournalLine and InventoryEntry are append-only and carry no `updated_*` or `version` fields; the two balance tables are caches that can always be rebuilt from the entries (R-INV-01).

| Account | `status` | Enum: Active, Blocked, Inactive | Y | Blocked accepts no new postings. |

A credit note uses the exchange rate of the invoice it credits, so crediting never creates an exchange difference.

**Reservation**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id`, `item_id`, `warehouse_id` | references | Y |  |
| `lot_id` | → Lot | N | Only when a specific lot is promised. |

A reservation is a claim, not a ledger entry, so it is updated in place and audited (R-AUD-01).

**Caches** (rebuildable, checked by the invariant job)

| Entity | Key | Derived values |
|---|---|---|
| StockBalance | company, item, warehouse, lot, stock_status | `on_hand_base`, `reserved_base`, `last_inventory_entry_id` |
| ItemCostState | company, item | `quantity_base`, `inventory_value`, `average_cost` (numeric(28,10), informational), `last_inventory_entry_id` |

Both rows are also the lock targets that serialise concurrent issues and reservations of the same item; their place in the lock sequence is in the lock order table below (R-LED-08).

**Moving average cost algorithm** (R-INV-05), per company and item, in recording order:

1. **Inbound with a known cost** (AdjustmentIn with an entered unit cost): cost_amount = q x entered_unit_cost, rounded to the currency's minor unit; value = value + cost_amount; quantity = quantity + q.
2. **Inbound without an entered cost** (AdjustmentIn): while quantity is above 0, cost_amount = q x value / quantity, computed exactly and then rounded to the currency's minor unit; at zero stock, cost_amount = q x the stored average_cost, rounded the same way. Rejected when the item has no stock and no average yet.
3. **Outbound** (Issue, AdjustmentOut): if the movement empties the stock, cost_amount = the full remaining value (R-INV-07). Otherwise cost_amount = q x value / quantity, computed exactly and then rounded. The stored average_cost is informational and never used for costing while quantity is above 0. Then value = value - cost_amount; quantity = quantity - q.
4. **Return** (ReturnIn): cost_amount = q x the unit cost of the original issue (D-11), then as step 1.
5. **Status change** (StatusOut, StatusIn): quantity moves between statuses; value and average are unchanged (R-INV-08).
6. After every movement that leaves quantity above 0, average_cost = value / quantity, rounded half away from zero to 10 decimals (numeric(28,10)). The stored value is informational, except as the fallback in step 2 at zero stock. When quantity reaches 0, value is 0 (R-INV-07) and the last average_cost is kept for step 2.

Costing follows recording order, not posting date. A back-dated posting in an open period takes the cost state at the moment it is recorded; there is no retroactive revaluation in v1 (R-INV-09).

**Lock order** (R-LED-08). Every command takes its locks class by class in this sequence. Within a class, rows are locked in one SQL statement, ordered by the key this table states for the class. A phase specification that needs a new lock class adds its row here before the class is used.

| Order | Lock class | Within the class | From |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The command's own document or master data row | One row, locked by its versioned update (If-Match) | Phase 0, milestone 1 |
| 2 | ItemCostState | Missing rows first inserted in one INSERT ... SELECT ... ORDER BY item_id ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; then all rows locked with one SELECT ... ORDER BY item_id FOR UPDATE | Phase 0, milestone 1 |
| 3 | StockBalance | Missing rows inserted the same way, then locked with one SELECT ... ORDER BY company, item, warehouse, lot, stock status FOR UPDATE before they are updated | Phase 0, milestone 1 |
| 4 | Reservations and the source lines they claim | Id order | Phase 1 (specified there) |
| 5 | OpenItem | Id order | Phase 2 (specified there) |
| Last | NumberSeries | The series rows the command uses (for a posting: the document's series and the journal entry series), in primary key order; the gapless journal entry number is taken as the last step before commit | Phase 0, milestone 1 |

StockBalance rows written by a posting always belong to items whose ItemCostState row is already locked, so milestone 1 cannot deadlock. A concurrency test posts two adjustments on the same items in opposite line order.

One permission exists per command, so the permission list and the API surface cannot drift apart. Nine entities cover access, audit, idempotency and outbound events.

**Example conflict pairs for v1:** CUSTOMER.SET_CREDIT_LIMIT with SALES_ORDER.APPROVE_CREDIT; ACCOUNT.MAINTAIN with MANUAL_JOURNAL.POST; FISCAL_PERIOD.REOPEN with MANUAL_JOURNAL.POST.

## State machines, part 1: master data and fiscal periods

All master data shares one lifecycle, and nothing is ever deleted (R-MD-03). Fiscal periods move one way to Closed, with a single step back from SoftClosed.

Each transition table reads: from state, command, to state, the guards that must hold, and the effects. A command whose guard fails is rejected with the rule ID (R-API-03).

**Master data lifecycle** (Party, PartyRole, ItemCompany, Warehouse, Account; Company and Contact use only Active and Inactive)

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE | Active | Required attributes valid; duplicate check passed, or overridden with permission (R-MD-01) | Audit event |
| Active | BLOCK | Blocked | Reason given | No new documents, lines or postings. Released documents may still complete, so goods are not trapped. An Account in Blocked rejects all postings. |
| Blocked | UNBLOCK | Active |  |  |
| Active, Blocked | DEACTIVATE | Inactive | No open documents, no stock on hand, no open items, no active reservations | Hidden from selection lists |
| Inactive | REACTIVATE | Active |  |  |
| Inactive | ANONYMISE (Person parties and contacts only) | Inactive | Statutory retention period for linked records has passed | Personal data replaced; `anonymised_at` set; audit values masked |

**Changing master data**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Active, Blocked | UPDATE | (unchanged) | Current version; sensitive fields need their own permission, for example `credit_limit` needs CUSTOMER.SET_CREDIT_LIMIT | Effective-dated fields get a new validity period (R-MD-02); audit event |

**Lot**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE | Released | Item is lot-tracked |  |
| Released | BLOCK_LOT | Blocked | Reason given | Reservations that now exceed available stock are released, latest-released first, and return to backorder (keeps I-05) |
| Blocked | RELEASE_LOT | Released | Reason given | ALLOCATE_BACKORDERS runs |

**FiscalYear**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE_YEAR | Open | Contiguous with the previous year | Creates its periods, all Open |
| Open | CLOSE_YEAR | Closed | All its periods Closed | Not available in v1 until the year-end result transfer is specified (see open questions). |

**FiscalPeriod**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open | SOFT_CLOSE | SoftClosed | VALIDATE_POSTING_PROFILE reports no gaps | Postings need the FISCAL_PERIOD.POST_SOFT_CLOSED permission |
| SoftClosed | REOPEN | Open | FISCAL_PERIOD.REOPEN permission; reason given | Audit event |
| SoftClosed | CLOSE | Closed | All earlier periods Closed; reconciliation invariants I-06 and I-07 pass | Final in v1 (R-PER-01) |

## State machines, part 2: kernel documents

Three kernel documents let Phase 0 put stock in, take it out and block it before any sales or purchasing exists; VAT_SETTLEMENT and OPENING_OPEN_ITEMS are built with finance in Phase 2. All five follow one pattern: Draft, then Posted, then optionally Reversed.

**Shared rules for every document type**

- CREATE gives status Draft and a `draft_reference`. UPDATE is allowed only in Draft and only on the current `version` (R-DOC-02, R-API-02).
- DISCARD moves a Draft to Discarded for types numbered on post. Types numbered on create (sales order, delivery, return) use CANCEL instead, so every issued number stays accounted for. Nothing is deleted (R-DOC-06).
- POST and every later transition write the status change, ledger effects, audit event and outbox event in one transaction (R-LED-05).
- REVERSE never edits the original. It creates opposite entries dated on a reversal posting date that must be in an open period (R-LED-01, R-LED-04).

**MANUAL_JOURNAL**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | At least 2 lines; amounts sum to 0 (R-LED-02); no control accounts (R-ACC-01); all accounts Active; period open (R-LED-04) | Gapless number; JournalEntry and lines; event JOURNAL_POSTED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | Reason given | Reversing JournalEntry with negated amounts, linked through `reversal_of_entry_id` |

**INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT** (a positive line quantity adds stock, a negative one removes it)

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | Items Stocked, and Active in the document's company (ItemCompany, D-43); lot given for lot-tracked items; outbound lines covered by stock in the line's stock status, and Available stock is not reserved (R-INV-03); entered_unit_cost given on inbound lines when the item has no average cost yet; reason code given; period open | InventoryEntries (AdjustmentIn, AdjustmentOut) costed by the moving average algorithm; JournalEntry per posting events E-01 and E-02; caches updated; event INVENTORY_ADJUSTED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | The reversal must not make stock negative | Outbound lines come back in at their original cost. Inbound lines go out as outbound movements costed by the algorithm (step 3, including R-INV-07), so stock value can never turn negative. A reversing JournalEntry posts the resulting amounts to the original accounts (R-PP-03) |

**STOCK_STATUS_CHANGE** (each line: item, lot, warehouse, from status, to status, quantity)

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | The from-status holds enough stock; when moving out of Available, the quantity is not reserved | StatusOut and StatusIn entries with zero value; no JournalEntry (R-INV-08); event STOCK_STATUS_CHANGED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | The opposite move is possible | Opposite status entries |

**VAT_SETTLEMENT** (one per company and period)

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | The period is SoftClosed; every earlier period is settled | Gapless number; JournalEntry per E-12 moves each tax code's OUTPUT_VAT balance for the period to VAT_SETTLEMENT; event VAT_SETTLED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | The period is not Closed; reason given | Reversing JournalEntry |

**OPENING_OPEN_ITEMS** (customer balances taken over at go-live)

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | Each line gives customer role, original document number, dates, currency, rate and open amount; period open | One OpenItem per line; JournalEntry per E-13; event OPENING_ITEMS_POSTED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | None of its open items is settled; reason given | Its open items reversed; reversing JournalEntry |

**Two ways to block stock.** `Lot.status` = Blocked blocks every unit of a lot, for example while a supplier certificate is missing. `stock_status` = Blocked blocks a specific quantity in a warehouse, for example damaged goods from a return. Available-to-promise excludes both (R-INV-04).

## State machines, part 3: sales order

The sales order is the only sales document with a branching lifecycle: credit control can stop it, and shipping can complete it in one step or several. It never posts to the ledgers itself; it only reserves stock.

*[Diagram in the live document: SALES_ORDER · 7 states]*

**SALES_ORDER**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE | Draft | Customer role Active | Order number assigned |
| Draft | RELEASE | Released | Customer and role Active; at least 1 line; every line priced (R-O2C-06) and taxable by exactly one rule (R-TAX-03); exchange rate available; credit check passes (R-O2C-01) | Prices, tax, addresses and rate stored on the order (R-DOC-05); reservations up to available-to-promise, remainder is backorder (R-O2C-02); `credit_check_result` = Passed; event SALES_ORDER_RELEASED |
| Draft | RELEASE | CreditBlocked | As above, but the credit check fails | `credit_check_result` = Failed; no reservations; event SALES_ORDER_CREDIT_BLOCKED |
| CreditBlocked | APPROVE_CREDIT | Released | SALES_ORDER.APPROVE_CREDIT permission (R-SEC-02) | `credit_check_result` = Approved, `credit_approved_by` set; reservations as on release |
| CreditBlocked | REOPEN | Draft |  |  |
| Released | REOPEN | Draft | No delivery linked to the order, except Cancelled or Discarded ones | Reservations released |
| Released, PartlyDelivered | (system, on shipment) | PartlyDelivered | Open quantity remains on at least one line | Reservations reduced by shipped quantity |
| Released, PartlyDelivered | (system, on shipment) | Delivered | Every line fully shipped or closed | Reservations Consumed |
| PartlyDelivered | CLOSE_SHORT | Delivered | Reason given; no open delivery for the remaining quantity | Remaining line quantity Closed; reservations Released |
| Delivered | (system, on invoice posting) | Closed | All shipped quantity invoiced | Event SALES_ORDER_CLOSED |
| Draft, CreditBlocked, Released | CANCEL | Cancelled | Nothing shipped; no delivery linked except Cancelled or Discarded ones; reason given | Reservations released; event SALES_ORDER_CANCELLED |

**Backorders.** Whenever available stock increases (an inbound adjustment, a return into Available, a status change to Available, or released reservations), the system command ALLOCATE_BACKORDERS reserves it for open order lines by requested date, then release time (R-O2C-02).

**Changing a released order.** An AMEND command is deferred. In v1, REOPEN an order with nothing shipped, or CLOSE_SHORT the rest and create a new order.

## State machines, part 4: delivery, invoice, credit note, payment, return

Shipped deliveries, posted invoices and posted credit notes are final; they are corrected only by a follow-on document (return or credit note), never by reversal. Only payments can be reversed, because a bank payment can genuinely bounce.

**DELIVERY**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE_FROM_ORDER | Draft | Order Released or PartlyDelivered; line quantity within open order quantity plus tolerance (R-DOC-03); a complete-delivery-only order includes all open quantity (R-O2C-03) | Links of type Fulfils |
| Draft | START_PICKING | Picking |  |  |
| Picking | BACK_TO_DRAFT | Draft |  |  |
| Draft, Picking | CONFIRM_SHIPMENT | Shipped | Shipped quantity per line given and not above the line quantity; lot given for lot-tracked items; shipped quantity not above this line's reservation plus unreserved available-to-promise (R-INV-03, I-05); a complete-delivery-only order ships all its open quantity (R-O2C-03); period open | `shipped_at` set; Fulfils link quantity set to the shipped quantity; Issue entries at moving average cost; JournalEntry per E-03; reservations reduced or Consumed; order status updated; event GOODS_ISSUED |
| Draft, Picking | CANCEL | Cancelled | Reason given | Links no longer count toward open quantity; reservations stay with the order |

A line shipped short leaves its remaining quantity open on the order line.

**CUSTOMER_INVOICE**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE_FROM_DELIVERIES | Draft | Delivery lines Shipped and not fully invoiced (R-O2C-05); one customer role, currency and bill-to address | Links of type Bills; prices copied from the order lines |
| Draft | POST | Posted | Exactly one tax rule per line (R-TAX-03); period open | Gapless number (R-DOC-04); tax calculated and rounded per the company's tax rounding level; due date; positive OpenItem; JournalEntry per E-04; order moved to Closed when fully invoiced; event INVOICE_POSTED |
| Posted, PartlyPaid | (system, on settlement) | PartlyPaid | Open amount between 0 and original |  |
| Posted, PartlyPaid | (system, on settlement) | Paid | Open amount 0 |  |
| PartlyPaid, Paid | (system, on settlement reversal) | Posted or PartlyPaid |  |  |

"Paid" means settled, by payments, credit notes or both. Charge lines (surcharge, freight) may be added in Draft with the INVOICE.ADD_CHARGE permission.

**CREDIT_NOTE**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE_FROM_INVOICE | Draft | Invoice Posted, PartlyPaid or Paid | Links of type Corrects |
| Draft | POST | Posted | Credited quantity or amount per invoice line not above invoiced minus already credited (R-O2C-08); reason code given; period open | Gapless number from the credit note series; tax at the original line's tax code, not re-determined (R-DOC-05); negative OpenItem, settled automatically against the invoice's open amount; JournalEntry per E-05; event CREDIT_NOTE_POSTED |

**CUSTOMER_PAYMENT**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | POST | Posted | Amount above 0; currency equals the bank account's currency; each allocation not above the open item's open amount; allocations sum not above the payment amount; period open | JournalEntry per E-06; negative OpenItem for the full amount; one Settlement per allocation; an allowed difference written off per E-07 (R-O2C-07); any unallocated amount stays on account; event PAYMENT_POSTED |
| Posted | REVERSE | Reversed | Reason given, for example a returned payment; period open | Settlements reversed with their E-07 and E-11 entries (R-OI-02); reversing JournalEntry; invoices return to their earlier status; event PAYMENT_REVERSED |

An on-account amount or an unsettled credit note is matched later with the SETTLE_OPEN_ITEMS command, which creates Settlements between a negative and a positive open item of the same customer role and currency. UNSETTLE reverses one settlement (R-OI-02). Refunding a customer's credit balance needs outgoing payments and is deferred to Phase 2.

**CUSTOMER_RETURN**

| From | Command | To | Guards | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | CREATE_FROM_DELIVERY | Draft | Delivery Shipped; return quantity not above shipped minus already returned (R-DOC-03) | Links of type Returns |
| Draft | RECEIVE | Received | Lot equals the lot originally shipped; target stock status chosen (Available or Blocked); period open | ReturnIn entries at the original issue's unit cost (D-11); JournalEntry per E-08; event RETURN_RECEIVED |
| Draft | CANCEL | Cancelled | Reason given |  |

A return does not create a credit note automatically; the credit note is a separate commercial decision.

## Posting profile: account roles and posting groups

Posting logic never names an account. It names an account role, and each company's posting profile maps that role to an account using the posting groups on the line. A new company, or a new country, therefore needs only configuration, never code (P-07).

**Account roles** (system-defined; Phases 0 to 2)

| Role | Meaning | Mapping keys | Must map to a control account |
|---|---|---|---|
| INVENTORY | Value of stock on hand | item posting group | Yes |
| COGS | Cost of goods sold | item posting group, ship-to scope | No |
| REVENUE | Sales revenue, including charge lines | item posting group, ship-to scope, tax code | No |
| RECEIVABLES | Amounts customers owe | party posting group | Yes |
| OUTPUT_VAT | VAT charged on sales | tax code | Yes |
| BANK | Money in the bank | none: taken from `BankAccount.gl_account_id` | No |
| PAYMENT_DIFFERENCE | Small differences written off at settlement | none | No |
| REALISED_FX | Exchange gains and losses realised at settlement | none | No |
| ROUNDING | Residue from currency conversion in one entry | none | No |
| INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT | Counterpart of stock adjustments | item posting group, reason code | No |
| VAT_SETTLEMENT | Account a period's VAT is moved to before it is reported and paid | none | No |
| OPENING_BALANCE | Clearing account for balances taken over at go-live | none | No |

Added with purchasing: GOODS_RECEIVED_NOT_INVOICED in Phase 1 (goods receipt); PAYABLES, INPUT_VAT and PURCHASE_PRICE_VARIANCE in Phase 2 (supplier invoices).

**Posting groups** (the mapping keys)

| Key | Where it lives | Values |
|---|---|---|
| Item posting group | `Item``Company``.item_posting_group`, validated against the ItemPostingGroup list (code, name) | Configurable, for example TRADE_GOODS, FREIGHT |
| Party posting group | `PartyRole.party_posting_group` | Fixed: Domestic, EU, NonEU |
| Ship-to scope | Derived per line from company country and ship-to country, exactly as for TaxRule | Fixed: Domestic, EU, NonEU |
| Tax code | The line's resolved `tax_code_id` | Per company, for example SE25 |
| Reason code | Inventory adjustment header | Fixed: OpeningBalance, CountDifference, Scrap, Other |

Charge lines (freight, small-order surcharge) reference a Service item such as FREIGHT, so they resolve REVENUE through that item's posting group.

**PostingProfileRule**

| Attribute | Type | Req | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `company_id` | → Company | Y |  |
| `account_role` | Code | Y | One of the roles above. |
| `item_posting_group`, `party_posting_group`, `tax_code_id`, `reason_code` | as above | N | Empty means "any value". Rules also carry ship_to_scope (Domestic, EU, NonEU), used by REVENUE and COGS. |
| `account_id` | → Account | Y | Must be Active. Control roles map only to control accounts and other roles only to non-control accounts (R-PP-04). |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | Date | Y, N | No two rules with the same role and the same key values may overlap in time. |

## Posting profile: the resolution algorithm

**Status (D-31).** Account and tax determination stay the decision tables below (D-35, refining D-31). The expression language is used for guards, validation, defaulting and pricing conditions, not for account mapping. R-PP-01 to R-PP-05 stay as they are.

For every journal line the engine picks exactly one account, or rejects the whole command; it never guesses. The most specific valid rule wins, with a fixed key order so that two rules can never tie (R-PP-01, D-19).

1. **Collect candidates:** rules for the same company and account role, valid on the posting date, where every non-empty key equals the line's value.
2. **Rank by specificity**, comparing keys in this fixed order: item posting group, then party posting group or ship-to scope (each role uses at most one of the two), then tax code, then reason code. A rule that sets an earlier key always beats one that leaves it empty, whatever the later keys hold.
3. **Pick the top candidate.** It is always unique, because two rules with the same keys cannot be valid at the same time.
4. **No candidate:** reject the command with R-PP-02 and name the role and the line's keys, for example "no account for REVENUE, item group TRADE_GOODS, ship-to scope EU, tax code SE25, posting date 2027-03-14".
5. **Record the result** on the journal line: `account_role` and `posting_rule_id` (P-05, explainability).
6. **Reversals do not resolve again.** A reversing entry copies the accounts of the lines it reverses, even if the mapping has changed since (R-PP-03).
7. **BANK** skips the rules and takes the account of the document's bank account.

**Currency conversion and rounding.** Each journal line is converted from transaction to company currency at the document's stored rate and rounded per line. If the entry then does not sum to 0, one ROUNDING line takes the residue. A residue larger than half a minor unit per line is a defect and is rejected (I-13).

**Example for REVENUE**, company SE01

| Item posting group | Ship-to scope | Account | Matches a line with TRADE_GOODS, EU? |
|---|---|---|---|
| TRADE_GOODS | Domestic | 3001 | No: ship-to scope differs |
| TRADE_GOODS | EU | 3108 | Yes, and most specific: chosen |
| TRADE_GOODS | (any) | 3001 | Yes, but less specific |
| (any) | EU | 3108 | Yes, but ranks below every rule that sets the item group |

**REVENUE and tax code (D-22 as amended).** REVENUE rules also carry the tax code, because ship-to scope alone cannot follow VAT treatment (R-TAX-01). An EU customer without VAT registration is taxed with SE25, so its line has the keys TRADE_GOODS, EU, SE25. With the BAS profile below, neither (TRADE_GOODS, EU, SE_EU_GOODS) nor (TRADE_GOODS, Domestic, SE25) matches it, so the command is rejected with R-PP-02 until a rule (TRADE_GOODS, EU, SE25) maps it, rather than posting to the EU revenue account. A REVENUE rule keyed by ship-to scope without a tax code, such as (TRADE_GOODS, EU, any), would match first and hide that gap, so REVENUE rules should always set the tax code. The configuration check below finds such gaps in advance.

**Configuration check.** The VALIDATE_POSTING_PROFILE command lists every combination of active item groups, party groups, ship-to scopes, tax codes and reason codes that would fail step 4. It also warns when the key order lets one rule hide another, for example a (TRADE_GOODS, any) rule hiding an (any, EU) rule. It runs before go-live, after any change to the profile, as a guard on SOFT_CLOSE, and on every command that creates or changes an item posting group, party posting group or tax code; such a command is rejected if the profile would become incomplete (R-PP-05). A gap therefore stops a master data change, never a shipment (D-24, D-32).

## Posting rules per event

Thirteen posting events cover Phases 0 to 2 on the sales side (goods-receipt events follow with the Phase 1 purchasing specification, supplier invoice and payment events with Phase 2); each one debits and credits the same amount, so every entry balances before rounding. Revenue and cost lines are written per document line so reports can analyse them by item (P-08); VAT is written per tax code.

| ID | Event and trigger | Debit (role, keys) | Credit (role, keys) | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-01 | Inventory adjustment in (POST, positive line) | INVENTORY (item group) | INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT (item group, reason) | Line cost |
| E-02 | Inventory adjustment out (POST, negative line) | INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT (item group, reason) | INVENTORY (item group) | Line cost |
| E-03 | Goods issue (delivery CONFIRM_SHIPMENT) | COGS (item group, ship-to scope) | INVENTORY (item group) | Line cost at moving average |
| E-04 | Customer invoice (POST) | RECEIVABLES (party group): gross total | REVENUE (item group, ship-to scope, tax code): net per line; OUTPUT_VAT (tax code): tax per tax code | Invoice amounts |
| E-05 | Credit note (POST) | REVENUE (item group, ship-to scope, tax code): net per line; OUTPUT_VAT (tax code): tax per tax code | RECEIVABLES (party group): gross total | Credit note amounts |
| E-06 | Customer payment (POST) | BANK (bank account) | RECEIVABLES (party group) | Payment amount |
| E-07 | Payment difference within tolerance (at settlement) | PAYMENT_DIFFERENCE | RECEIVABLES (party group) | Difference; signs swap when the customer overpaid |
| E-08 | Customer return (RECEIVE) | INVENTORY (item group) | COGS (item group, ship-to scope) | Original issue cost |
| E-09 | Manual journal (POST) | Accounts on the lines | Accounts on the lines | Line amounts; no roles; control accounts refused (R-ACC-01) |
| E-10 | Rounding residue (any entry) | ROUNDING, or credit | ROUNDING, or debit | Residue after per-line conversion |
| E-11 | Realised exchange difference (at settlement of foreign-currency items) | RECEIVABLES (party group) or REALISED_FX | REALISED_FX or RECEIVABLES (party group) | Difference between the company-currency values of the two settled portions |
| E-12 | VAT settlement (POST VAT_SETTLEMENT for a period) | OUTPUT_VAT (tax code): the period's balance per tax code | VAT_SETTLEMENT | Net OUTPUT_VAT postings dated in the period |
| E-13 | Opening open item (POST OPENING_OPEN_ITEMS) | RECEIVABLES (party group) | OPENING_BALANCE | Open amount at go-live, per item; signs swap for a credit balance |

**Not posted to the general ledger:** order release (reservation only), stock status changes (R-INV-08), and settlements without a difference.

**Worked example for E-11.** An invoice of EUR 100 is posted at rate 11.00 (receivables +1,100 SEK). The payment of EUR 100 arrives at rate 11.50 (bank +1,150 SEK, receivables -1,150 SEK). After settlement both open items are 0 in EUR, but receivables show -50 SEK, so E-11 posts receivables debit 50 and REALISED_FX credit 50. Receivables are back at 0 and match the open items (I-07).

**Reversals** post the original lines with opposite signs and the original accounts (R-PP-03).

## Example account mapping for Sweden (BAS)

If Sweden is confirmed as the first localisation (D-13), the default profile maps to the BAS 2026 chart for a trading company. Seven roles have a clear BAS account; the cost-of-goods and adjustment accounts need an accountant's choice (D-20).

Account names are as written in [BAS kontoplan 2026 v2](https://www.bas.se/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/BAS_kontoplan_2026_v2.pdf).

| Role | Keys | BAS account | BAS name | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| INVENTORY | TRADE_GOODS | 1460 | Lager av handelsvaror | Proposed |
| RECEIVABLES | any | 1510 | Kundfordringar | Proposed |
| BANK | via BankAccount | 1930 | Företagskonto | Proposed |
| OUTPUT_VAT | SE25 | 2611 | Utgående moms på försäljning inom Sverige, 25 % | Proposed |
| REVENUE | TRADE_GOODS, Domestic, SE25 | 3001 | Försäljning inom Sverige, 25 % moms | Proposed |
| REVENUE | TRADE_GOODS, EU, SE_EU_GOODS | 3108 | Försäljning varor till annat EU-land, momsfri | Proposed |
| REVENUE | TRADE_GOODS, NonEU, SE_EXPORT | 3105 | Försäljning varor till land utanför EU | Proposed |
| ROUNDING, PAYMENT_DIFFERENCE | none | 3740 | Öres- och kronutjämning | Proposed for small differences |
| COGS | TRADE_GOODS | 4010 (Inköp av handelsvaror i Sverige) or 4960 (Förändring av lager av handelsvaror) |  | Open: D-20 |
| INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT | by reason | To be chosen |  | Open: D-20 |
| REALISED_FX | none | To be chosen |  | Open: D-20 |

These mappings are configuration data in a localisation package, not code. They are not a compliance claim until an accountant has reviewed them.

## Invariants Claude Code must test

Fourteen invariants define "the books are correct". Each is an automated test after every command in property-based test runs, and a nightly check in production; any failure stops period close.

| ID | Invariant | Protects |
|---|---|---|
| I-01 | Every JournalEntry sums to 0 in company currency. | R-LED-02 |
| I-02 | No JournalLine or InventoryEntry has amount or quantity 0; lines that would be 0 (for example 0 % VAT) are not written. Txn and company amounts share a sign. | Data quality |
| I-03 | StockBalance on hand = sum of InventoryEntry quantity per key, and is never below 0 in a warehouse that does not allow negative stock (the default, R-INV-03). | R-INV-01, R-INV-03 |
| I-04 | ItemCostState value and quantity = sums of InventoryEntry cost and quantity per company and item; value is 0 when quantity is 0. | R-INV-05, R-INV-07 |
| I-05 | Active reservations per item and warehouse never exceed Available stock outside Blocked lots. | R-INV-04 |
| I-06 | General ledger balance of INVENTORY-role accounts = sum of InventoryEntry cost, per company, at any date. | R-INV-06, R-ACC-01 |
| I-07 | General ledger balance of RECEIVABLES-role accounts = sum of open receivable items in company currency, per company, at any date. | Sub-ledger integrity |
| I-08 | Every InventoryEntry with cost not 0 links to a JournalEntry; every posted document whose type posts to the GL and that has at least one non-zero amount has one. A document whose lines all have zero cost writes no journal entry. | R-INV-06, R-LED-05 |
| I-09 | Gapless series (invoices, credit notes, manual journals, journal entries per fiscal year) have no gaps or duplicates. | R-DOC-04, R-DOC-07 |
| I-10 | Linked follow-on quantity per source line never exceeds its quantity plus tolerance. | R-DOC-03 |
| I-11 | The application's database role can only INSERT and SELECT on JournalEntry, JournalLine, InventoryEntry and AuditEvent. | R-LED-01, R-LED-06 |
| I-12 | Open amount = original amount minus non-reversed settlements, and never changes sign. | Settlement integrity |
| I-13 | A ROUNDING line never exceeds half a minor unit per converted line in its entry. | R-MON-02 |
| I-14 | Each module role is refused every write outside its own schema, the login role is refused every table write, and no role can UPDATE or DELETE ledger or audit tables. An integration test attempts each forbidden write and expects a database error. | R-DB-01, R-LED-06 |

**Scenario catalogue (to write next):** opening balance, sale with full and partial delivery, backorder allocation, credit block and approval, invoice and payment with a difference, EUR invoice with exchange difference, credit note, return into Blocked stock, period soft close and close.

## New rules and decisions introduced by this spec

This spec adds 17 rules and 9 decisions. Both are mirrored into the foundation doc, which stays the single catalogue of rules and decisions.

**Rules**

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| R-UOM-01 | An item unit's factor is immutable once used on a posted document; a different factor needs a new unit code. |
| R-TAX-03 | Exactly one tax rule must match a line; zero or several matches rejects the command. |
| R-DOC-06 | A Draft can be discarded (or cancelled, for types numbered on create) but never deleted. |
| R-DOC-07 | A gapless number is taken inside the posting transaction under a row lock on its series. |
| R-ACC-01 | Control accounts accept postings only from their sub-ledger or the system documents VAT_SETTLEMENT and OPENING_OPEN_ITEMS, never from manual journals. |
| R-INV-07 | An issue that empties an item's stock takes the item's full remaining value. |
| R-INV-08 | A stock status change moves quantity between statuses with zero value and no journal entry. |
| R-INV-09 | Costing follows recording order; there is no retroactive revaluation in v1. |
| R-PER-01 | A Closed fiscal period is final in v1. |
| R-API-04 | Reusing an idempotency key with a different request is rejected. |
| R-PP-01 | The most specific valid posting rule wins, with keys ranked: item posting group, party posting group or ship-to scope, tax code, reason code. |
| R-PP-02 | A line with no matching posting rule rejects the command, naming the role and the keys. |
| R-PP-03 | Reversals reuse the original lines' accounts and never resolve again. |
| R-PP-04 | Control roles map only to control accounts; other roles map only to non-control accounts. |
| R-LED-06 | The application's database role has no UPDATE or DELETE rights on ledger and audit tables. |
| R-OI-01 | When a settlement closes an open item, its company-currency value is the item's full remaining company amount, so no residue stays behind. |
| R-OI-02 | Reversing a settlement also reverses its write-off (E-07) and exchange difference (E-11) entries. |

**Decisions**

| ID | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| D-14 | Product name: Themis, with Jozen as the working brand | Decided 2026-10-08; trademark check pending, because Themis is already used by governance, risk and compliance software |
| D-15 | Journal amounts are signed, debit positive, instead of separate debit and credit columns | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-16 | Type-specific header fields live in one-to-one extension tables, not JSON | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-17 | Identifiers are UUID v7 | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-18 | Stock status (Available, Blocked) is part of the stock balance key | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-19 | Posting rule key order: item posting group, party posting group or ship-to scope, tax code, reason code | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-20 | Swedish accounts for COGS, inventory adjustments and realised exchange differences | Open: choose with an accountant |
| D-21 | Foreign-currency documents are allowed from the first business phase, with realised exchange differences posted at settlement (E-11) | Decided (foundation decision log) |
| D-22 | REVENUE is keyed by item posting group, ship-to scope and tax code; COGS by item posting group and ship-to scope | Decided (foundation decision log), amended 2026-10-09 |

**Open questions for the next round**

- Price lookup when the order unit has no price line: convert from the base-unit price, or reject?
- Should receiving a return offer to create the credit note in the same step?
- VAT treatment of payment differences above a few kronor, if the tolerance is ever raised.
- Year-end result transfer and opening balances for a new fiscal year (needed before the first year closes).
